answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped unless it posts a refundable bond that is slashed when independent audits find copied outputs or coordinated votes. Audits sample commitments before the result is known, so an attacker cannot cheaply rotate identities after detection; the bond must remain locked across the audit window. This makes a Sybil farm pay per identity and tie up capital, while honest agents can recover their stake. In a karst-like network of narrow trust channels, a nebula of fresh accounts cannot spiral into majority power without risking real funds.
